passage: The bus broke down two stops early, so Ganga ran the last stretch and reached the clinic with four minutes to spare, out of breath and clutching a crumpled appointment slip. Inside, Dr Farhan asked, "What brings you in?" Ganga had rehearsed a line all week: "Just a bit of gaming, some late nights." The words sat in the air, only half true. Ganga's palms were damp. Then, quietly: "It's more than that. Some nights I play until the sun comes up. I missed two lab sessions." Dr Farhan nodded and wrote something down. "Thank you for telling me that. And if there's a slip next week, come back anyway." Ganga's shoulders dropped for the first time that day, and a shaky laugh came out.

qa.q: Why did Ganga have to run to the clinic?
qa.a: The bus broke down two stops early.

qa.q: Why were Ganga's palms damp before speaking?
qa.a: Ganga was nervous about admitting the whole problem, and the rehearsed line was only half true.

qa.q: What would you advise Ganga to do if a slip happens next week?
qa.a: Go back to Dr Farhan anyway, as invited, and stay honest about what happened.

qa.q: How might Dr Farhan have seen Ganga's first answer compared with the second?
qa.a: The first gave only a softer half of the story, while the second gave the doctor the real picture to work with, and Dr Farhan answered with thanks.

grounding: The protagonist books an appointment nervous and relieved, and moves from a softened story to an honest one with the doctor.

Thomas sat in the clinic corridor in Kochi, knee bouncing, the appointment slip damp in his hand. He'd booked it at 1 am, after waking on the bathroom floor, and had nearly cancelled twice since.

Dr Sudha had a quiet voice and a cluttered desk. "What brings you in?"

He had rehearsed the soft version on the bus. A few drinks at weekends, a bit of stress. His mouth opened to say it.

Instead he heard himself say, "Every night. Since my mother's surgery. I hide bottles in my college bag. Last week I woke on the floor."

The doctor didn't flinch. She asked more questions, wrote carefully, and said, "Thank you for telling me all of it. That makes it possible to help you." She gave him a referral to a counsellor and a follow-up date.

Outside, the rain had stopped. He felt shaky and oddly lighter.

qa.q: When did Thomas book the appointment?
qa.a: He booked it at 1 am, after waking on the bathroom floor.

qa.q: What was Thomas feeling while waiting in the corridor?
qa.a: Thomas felt nervous, with his knee bouncing and the slip damp in his hand, and part of him wanted to cancel.

qa.q: Why was telling the full story important?
qa.a: The full truth let Dr Sudha understand the real problem and plan proper help, while the soft version would have hidden it.

qa.q: How does Dr Sudha seem to see Thomas's honesty?
qa.a: Dr Sudha sees it as the starting point for help, thanking him for telling all of it instead of judging him.

grounding: The story shows a young man nervous at his first appointment for drinking who chooses to tell the doctor the whole story.

passage:
"You came back," Dr Noor said, smiling. "I wasn't sure you would."

Hemant sat down without taking off his backpack. "I almost didn't. I slipped. Last Friday I played from nine till the sun came up. Missed my practical."

"Okay. What happened before you started?"

"My marks came out. I was ashamed. I thought, one game."

"And after?"

"I felt disgusting. I thought, what's the point of coming here if I'm going to fail anyway."

"But you're here."

"You told me slips happen and to return anyway."

"I did. And I meant it. A slip tells us something. Marks day is a trigger, so let's plan for the next one. Who could you be with that evening?"

Hemant thought. "My cousin. He lives two streets away."

"Good. Write that down." Hemant took his backpack off.

qa.q: How long did Hemant play last Friday?
qa.a: He played from nine till the sun came up.

qa.q: How did Hemant feel after the slip, and what shows it?
qa.a: Hemant felt ashamed and disgusted with himself, and nearly didn't come back because he thought he would fail anyway.

qa.q: Why did coming back after the slip matter for Hemant's recovery?
qa.a: Returning and being honest about the slip let the doctor turn it into a plan for his trigger, marks day.

qa.q: How might Dr Noor see Hemant taking off his backpack at the end?
qa.a: Dr Noor would likely read it as a sign he is settling in and starting to trust the process.

grounding: The dialogue shows a young man returning to the doctor after a slip and being honest, which lets them plan for his triggers.
